summary: This Wikipedia article surveys Earth rainfall climatology, the study of how precipitation is distributed across the planet and what controls it, including air pressure, humidity, topography, cloud type and raindrop size. It covers global precipitation totals, the role of rainfall in the Köppen climate classification, and regional patterns for Africa, Asia, Australia, New Zealand, Europe, North America and South America, plus the urban heat island effect on rainfall.
one_line: Wikipedia overview of rainfall climatology: how precipitation is distributed globally, its controls, and regional rainfall patterns across continents.
key_facts: Earth rainfall climatology aims to measure, understand and predict rain distribution across regions of Earth via direct measurement and remote sensing.
Current technologies accurately predict rainfall 3–4 days in advance using numerical weather prediction.
Approximately 505,000 cubic kilometres of water falls as precipitation each year, with 398,000 cubic kilometres of it over the oceans.
The globally averaged annual precipitation is 990 millimetres (39 in).
Most of Australia is semi-arid or desert, making it the world's driest continent (excluding Antarctica).
Cherrapunji, on the southern slopes of the Eastern Himalaya in Shillong, India, has an average annual rainfall of 11,430 mm (450 in).
Mount Bellenden Ker in north-east Australia records an average of 8,000 millimetres (310 in) per year.
Cropp River in New Zealand has a 11499mm per year average, described as the 4th highest rainfall in the world.
Lloró, a town in Chocó, Colombia, averages 13,300 mm per year (523.6 in) and is probably the place with the largest measured rainfall in the world.
Quibdó, capital of Chocó, receives 9,000 millimetres (350 in) per year, the most rain among cities with over 100,000 inhabitants.
The Big Bog on the island of Maui receives on average 404 inches (10,300 mm) every year, the wettest location in the US.
Rainfall rates downwind of cities are increased between 48% and 116%, and some cities show a total precipitation increase of 51%.
Tropical cyclones track near and along the western Mexican coastline primarily between July and September.
Tutunendo, Colombia, averages 11,394 mm per year and received 26,303 mm in 1974, the largest annual rainfall measured in Colombia.
The Köppen classification depends on average monthly values of temperature and precipitation and has five primary types labeled A through E.
Rain forests are defined by minimum normal annual rainfall between 1,750 millimetres (69 in) and 2,000 millimetres (79 in).
In Europe, the wettest regions are in the Alps and downwind of bodies of water, particularly the Atlantic west coasts.
Mexico City receives an average of only 5 millimeters of rain during February but more than 160 millimeters in July.
